entries.title: Genesis 49:2
segments: We should desire not only to be useful in life, but in death to inculcate such truth, communicate such instruction, and set such an example as shall be most useful to coming generations.

entries.title: Genesis 49:3
segments: Excellency of dignity, and--of power; as the first-born, the blessings of the birthright belonged to Reuben, but on account of his sin it was taken from him.

entries.title: Genesis 49:4
segments:
Unstable as water; easily overcome by temptation, and rushing headlong into iniquity. 
 
  Shalt not excel; neither he nor his posterity would ever be distinguished.

entries.title: Genesis 49:5
segments:
Are brethren; not merely descended form the same parents, but alike in cruelty of disposition. 
 
  Instruments of cruelty; he refers to their destruction of the Shechemites,

entries.title: Genesis 49:6
segments: Come not thou; in this verse Jacob expresses his deep abhorrence of their crimes.

entries.title: Genesis 49:7
segments: I will divide them; this was a prophecy from God, that their posterity would be scattered among the other tribes.  The Simeonites never attained to distinction among the tribes of Israel.  They had their portion within the inheritance of Judah,

; and seem to have been gradually absorbed and lost in that powerful tribe.  The Levites, as is well known, received no separate inheritance among the other tribes, but were distributed in cities throughout the land. 
 
We may feel the effects of our sins long after they have been committed.  Even if they have been repented of and forgiven, we and our posterity may suffer evils in consequence of them to the end of time.

entries.title: Genesis 49:8
segments: Thy brethren shall praise; there is an allusion here to the meaning of the word Judah, that is, praise.

His descendants would be highly distinguished and honored by all the other tribes. 
 
  In the neck; they would overcome their enemies.

entries.title: Genesis 49:9
segments: A lion; as the lion is the king of the forest, and terrible to other beasts, so the tribe of Judah would govern the other tribes, and be a terror to their foes.

entries.title: Genesis 49:10
segments:
The septre; an emblem of power and authority. 
 
  Shiloh; the Messiah, Prince of peace, sent as a Saviour.

. 
 
  To him; to Shiloh. 
 
  The gathering of the people; or, the obedience of the people.  See

.  They shall accept him as their King, and he shall reign over them. 
 
The fact that the sceptre has long ago departed from the tribe of Judah, who have ceased to govern Israel, shows that the Messiah has come, and that the expectation of a future Messiah is vain.

entries.title: Genesis 49:12
segments: Red with wine--white with milk; his posterity would have a very fruitful country, and an abundance of the good things of life.

entries.title: Genesis 49:13
segments:
The haven of the sea; or, the shore of the sea.  The possessions of Zebulun extended from the sea of Chinnereth, afterwards called the sea of Galilee, on the east, to the Mediterranean on the west. 
 
  Zidon; or Sidon, a very ancient city on the Mediterranean, north of the more modern city of Tyre.

entries.title: Genesis 49:14
segments:
vv. 14-15 
 
  Issachar; the territory of Issachar lay south of Zebulun, and included the noble and fertile plain of Esdraelon. 
 
  Strong ass--bowed his shoulder to bear; his posterity would be distinguished for their ability and readiness to labor, for their quiet, patient, and industrious habits, and their preferring to live at home rather than engage in wars or public afairs.

entries.title: Genesis 49:16
segments: Judge his people; in allusion to the meaning of the word Dan, that is, one who judges.  From the tribe of Dan came Samson.

entries.title: Genesis 49:17
segments: A serpent--and adder; they would overcome their enemies by subtlety, stratagem, and surprise, rather than by courage and open force.

entries.title: Genesis 49:18
segments: The fulfilment of the prophecies uttered by Jacob on his death-bed shows that he spoke as directed by the Holy Ghost.  But however highly favored a good man may be on earth, however numerous his blessings or those of his posterity, nothing will fully satisfy him but the salvation of God.

entries.title: Genesis 49:19
segments: Gad; the possessions of the tribe of Gad lay on the east of the Jordan, and were peculiarly exposed to the assaults of hostile troops. See

entries.title: Genesis 49:20
segments: Fat--royal dainties; the inheritance of his posterity would yield in abundance, not merely the necessaries, but also the luxuries of life.

entries.title: Genesis 49:21
segments:
A hind let loose; a female deer roaming at large, distinguished for beauty and fleetness.  But some render, Naphtali is a slender deer, slender being used in the sense of graceful. 
 
  Goodly words; words graceful and pleasant. He is thus marked as excelling in the gift of speech.  Of this the Song of Deborah and Barak,
, is an example.

entries.title: Genesis 49:22
segments: A fruitful bough; he would have a very numerous posterity.

entries.title: Genesis 49:24
segments: From thence; some refer these words to Joseph, but they belong rather to God.  We may render the whole passage thus: From thence [even from] the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel; from the God of thy father, who helps thee; and from the Almighty, who blesses thee, [shall be] blessings of heaven above, etc.

entries.title: Genesis 49:25
segments:
Blessings of heaven above; the sunshine, and fertilizing rain and dews. 
 
  Blessings of the deep; the fertlizing springs and streams. 
 
  Blessings of the breasts and of the womb; fruitfulness in his posterity, and in their flocks and herds.

entries.title: Genesis 49:26
segments:
Have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors; have exceeded the blessings which my ancestors pronounced on their children.  The spirit of prophecy has made to me a fuller revelation of the good things reserved for thee. 
 
  Unto the utmost bound--everlasting hills; so long as they shall endure.  But many prefer to render, "Unto the precious things of the everlasting hills;" that is, my blessing extends so far as to include all these, and as long as they endure.  Compare

. 
 
The measures which men take in opposing God, are made the means of fulfilling his designs; and those which are adopted to prevent the exaltation and glory of his people, are made the occasion of promoting them.

entries.title: Genesis 49:27
segments: Raven as a wolf; his posterity would be warlike, fierce, and cruel.

entries.title: Genesis 49:28
segments: Blessed them; foretold the blessings God would bestow upon them, and what would take place in future times with regard to their posterity.

entries.title: Genesis 49:29
segments: In the cave;

entries.title: Genesis 49:33
segments: Men who have finished the work God gave them to do, and are through grace gathered in peace--their bodies to the grave and their souls to the assembly of just men made perfect--are unspeakably blessed. Re 14.13
